Ron Gardenhire was not short on words when talking about how he felt after being tossed during Wednesday's game against the A's.
Gardenhire was thrown out in the third inning after arguing balls and strikes during Niko Goodrum's at bat. Thursday, Gardenhire spoke on what happened.

“Niko was looking at him but I was yelling from the dugout. Two of the pitches were off the plate, we’re talking close, but off the plate," Gardnehire said. "I was just yelling ‘those balls are off the plate’ and he’s saying ‘no they’re not’ while the pitcher is still out on the mound, no they’re not. Finally the inning ended and I told him ‘you just (expletive) that kid’s at bat’ is basically what he did. That ends up a big at bat right there, he could have walked in that situation."
Gardenhire went onto explain that the Tigers have a TV in their dugout to see balls and Strikes, and bench coach Steve Liddle told him those were balls.

"In our little box (the balls were off the plate), but I don’t know what box the umpire sees, there might be a different box they -- it could be a little bit (expletive) wider. I just don’t know what box they see, but our box showed it off and we have the luxury of our video people right there so we can get everything. So all you got to do is one of my coaches walks in there (and says) ‘Ron that (expletive) ball is a ball’ then he gets me fired up and I yell at the umpire and the (expletive) throws me out. That’s what happened. He’s goes in there -- ‘Ronny, that was off the (expletive) plate’ ‘hey let’s (expletive) go (ump)’ ‘you’re gone.’ It’s (expletive) Steve Liddle doing all the (expletive). I haven’t moved from my seat, he threw me out and I was sitting right (expletive) here and I’m just going ‘you’re (expletive) wrong, those are balls, they’re are off the (expletive) plate.’ And it’s all because I had to listen to Steve Liddle.”
Liddle coached the Tigers the rest of the way, losing 3-0 to the A's. It was also Detroit' eighth straight loss -- their longest losing streak since last September.
Gardenhire's ejection from arguing balls and strikes ironically came the same day the Tigers fired former pitching coach Chris Bosio for 'insensitive comments.'
The Tigers hope to end their losing streak Thursday afternoon when they face the A's one last time at 1:10 p.m. ET.
